title: The Blue Jackal
blurb: A jackal falls in the dye vat and wakes up a king.
script:
[warmly] There was once a jackal who was always hungry, and always a little unlucky.

[curious] One evening he crept into a village looking for scraps… and the dogs saw him. [excited] They barked! They chased him! He ran and ran, down one lane and up another… [surprised] and he did not see the great open vat standing in the dyer's yard.

[short pause] SPLASH.

[amused] When he climbed out, dripping and spluttering… he was BLUE. [playfully] Not a little blue. Not blue in patches. [slowly] Blue as the sky just after the sun goes down.

[curious] He ran back to the forest, and every animal he passed stopped and stared. Nobody had ever seen anything like him.

[worried] The tiger stepped back. The elephant did not know whether to bow. [whispers] The deer hid behind a tree and peeped out.

[thoughtful] And the jackal, who was clever, saw all this… and had an idea.

[grandly] “Do not be afraid,” he said. “I have been sent. The gods themselves made me this colour, and set me here to be your king.”

[surprised] And they believed him.

[cheerfully] They brought him the best of everything. He slept on soft leaves. The tiger fanned him. The peacock danced for him. [amused] He gave orders, and everybody followed them, and it was all very comfortable indeed.

[slyly] And the first thing he did as king… was send all the other jackals far away, out of the forest. [quietly] Because they might have known him.

[gently] The days went by. The blue jackal grew round and happy. [softly] But something was missing, and he could not say what.

[thoughtful] He would sit at night and listen to the forest… the owls, the frogs, the wind in the leaves… [sadly] and feel a small ache he did not have a name for.

[short pause] Then one evening, far away beyond the trees… the jackals began to howl.

[softly] It was the sound he had grown up with. The sound of his family, calling to the moon the way jackals have always called.

[gently] And before he could stop himself… before he even thought about it… [slowly] he lifted his head… and he howled back.

[surprised] The forest went very still.

[incredulous] The tiger turned. The elephant turned. [whispers] “That,” said the deer, “is a jackal.”

[worried] And the blue jackal looked around at all of them, and there was nothing at all he could say, because it was true. [short pause] So he ran.

[softly] He ran until the trees ended, and he found the other jackals under the moon, and they made room for him without asking a single question.

[warmly] The dye washed out, in time. [gently] And he was only a jackal again, hungry and a little unlucky. [long pause] [whispers] But he never had to pretend… ever again.
